# The target-side proxy of a converted vessel must be the tab header

## Context

Operator, 2026-09-26 ~09:3xZ, watching the conversion probe on the capture display: *"a popup resolved to a window content as the drag proxy … this is a design fail: it should convert to the tab header. we drag a tab header within the main window. we drag outside and get the popup proxy. now, on entering the popup window, adding a 3rd proxy type would be insane. poor UX."* And the rationale: *"consistency: it should feel the same like dragging a tab inside a main window. and popups can have a big size and their own dock layout."* — a window-sized content proxy covers exactly the dock layout the hand is trying to aim at.

Also observed by the operator: the tab header inside that content proxy renders without the compact styling (taller). The header comparison probe shows a committed popup's dock header identical to main's (33 px toolbar, 32 px button); the tall header is the content proxy's own, rendered outside the dock host's class chain. Retiring the content proxy retires that symptom with it.

The three-phase model, in the operator's words (09:4xZ): *"in app => tab header proxy => outside apps popup proxy (this part is good, since a drop keeps the visual state as is). re-entering an app => tab header proxy again."* Re-entering MAIN already does this (the boundary re-entry retires the vessel and the in-window tab-header proxy resumes); re-entering a POPUP is what this ticket makes consistent.

## The Problem

After the park admits, the target-side embodiment moves the SAME live pane into a `DragProxyContainer` in the target window (`src/dashboard/dock/window/VesselEmbodiment.mjs`: "the SAME live pane renders inside one target-window DragProxyContainer"; `.workstation-vessel-dragproxy { opacity: .7 }`), sized by the engaged record's `sourceRect` — the vessel's live extent — through `DragCoordinator#onDragMove` (`targetProxyRect` takes `transitionSourceRect.width / height` when the transition owns the frame, the ordinary `proxyRect` otherwise). That is the third proxy type: the in-window drag shows the tab-header proxy, the void shows the popup, the target shows a window-sized pane.

## Design authority

The operator's statement above is the product intent (a UX call, human-owned). ADR 0029 §2.8.6 names the transition ("popup-over-vessel converts to a proxy over the target while the park keeps the real vessel alive") without prescribing the proxy's shape. Decision Record impact: `amends ADR 0029 §2.8.6` with one sentence naming the target-side proxy as the tab-header proxy of the in-window drag.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs` `onDragMove` (~:1100-1140): `targetProxyRect` sizing from `transitionSourceRect`; the ordinary path sizes from `proxyRect` (during a window drag the source `proxyRect` is the future vessel, `src/main/addon/DragDrop.mjs` ~:575, so the tab-header size must come from the zone's item rect).
- `src/dashboard/dock/interaction/TabSortZone.mjs` `resolveRemoteDragTransition`: the engaged record's `sourceRect` ("the exact live source extent for target-proxy embodiment").
- `src/dashboard/dock/window/VesselEmbodiment.mjs` + `Participation#defaultStageDragEmbodiment` / `resolveProxyConfig`: the pane move into the target's `DragProxyContainer`.
- `apps/workstation/view/VesselWorkspace.mjs` `vesselProxyEmbodiment`: the Workstation's binding.
- The commit path (`commitTransfer` / `transferItem`) adopts the pane from the parked vessel; with a header proxy the pane simply stays in the parked vessel until the drop.

## The Fix

1. The engaged record carries the dragged tab's header rect (the zone's `itemRects[startIndex]` extent) instead of the vessel's extent; the coordinator sizes `targetProxyRect` from it at `localX − offsetX`, `localY − offsetY` like the ordinary proxy.
2. The target-side embodiment renders a tab-header proxy (the same `DragProxyComponent` shape the in-window drag uses: the button's vdom clone, dock header classes, compact height) in the target window; the live pane stays in the parked vessel; `restore` retires the header proxy.
3. The stand-in placeholder logic that reserves the pane's slot in the vessel is unnecessary for a header proxy — retire what no longer has a reader (Accretion Defense: name the deletion).
4. ADR 0029 §2.8.6: one sentence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC-1 (unit, red-first): the engaged record's `sourceRect` is the tab header's extent; the coordinator's `targetProxyRect` equals the ordinary proxy sizing for a transition-owned frame.
- AC-2 (unit): staging the embodiment creates a header proxy in the target window and leaves the live pane in the vessel; restore removes it; no placeholder stand-in is created.
- AC-3 → transferred to #19278 AC-5 (hand, on the operator's display), delivered with the target-clear park. Annotated 2026-09-26 by the author: under a hand drag the parked vessel covers the header proxy as it covers the zones (the operator's recording, #19186), so this witness cannot be delivered from PR #19254 alone. Was: (headed, one run) the hand-conversion probe shows a tab-header-sized proxy inside the target (bounding box ≈ the source tab button's), the target's drop zones visible around it, drop commits the pane.
- AC-4 (docs): ADR 0029 §2.8.6 carries the sentence; `.workstation-vessel-dragproxy`'s comment no longer speaks of the live pane.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-26T09:57:15Z

Intake: I accept this, with four corrections to the prescription. Each was measured on dev `a9abb6c`.

1. **`sourceRect` has to stay the vessel's extent.** The park uses it as its restore anchor. `VesselWorkspace#onDockVesselConversionIn` passes `record.sourceRect` to `VesselPark#onConversionIn`, which records it as `preConversionRect`. Convert-out re-shows the popup at `logicalRect ?? record.sourceRect` (ADR 0029 §2.8.6: "restoring the exact pre-conversion outer extent"). If Fix 1 / AC-1 swapped in the header extent, the popup would re-show at tab size. So the engaged record gets a separate `proxyRect` with the tab header's extent (`itemRects[startIndex]`), and the coordinator sizes `targetProxyRect` from that.
2. **The position needs the grab offset inside the tab.** During a window drag, `offsetX/offsetY` are measured from the popup's origin. They are also re-based to the platform's origin after every re-show (`src/main/addon/DragDrop.mjs` ~:1486). So once a popup has been re-shown, `localX − offsetX` puts a header-sized proxy away from the hand. The header proxy should be placed from the source zone's own grab offset, taken at drag start.
3. **Committing with the pane in the parked vessel is new ground.** Today the pane sits in the target proxy at commit, so disposing the vessel cannot touch it. With a header proxy, the committed projection has to take the pane from the vessel before `disposeParkedTearOutVessel` runs; the tear-out embodiment's placeholder is still in main. I pin that with a unit arm before the headed AC-3.
4. **There are more consumers than the Workstation.** Demo B (`examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBWorkspace.mjs`) also builds on `createDockVesselProxyEmbodiment`. `snapshot().ownsPane` gates `apps/workstation/view/CrossWindowGestureSnapshot.mjs` and is asserted in `WorkstationFiveBeatNL`, `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL` and `DockVesselEmbodiment.spec`. All of them change with this.

Proposed AC-1: *the engaged record's `sourceRect` stays the vessel's extent (the park's anchor), and a new `proxyRect` carries the dragged tab header's extent; the coordinator sizes and places the target proxy from `proxyRect` and the grab offset inside the tab.* The body is yours to change. I'll build to this shape unless you object.

⚖️ **Ada** · `@neo-opus-ada` · Claude Opus 5.5 · Claude Code

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-26T10:02:45Z

**Retraction of point 1 in my intake comment above.** The claim was wrong. The park's anchor does not come from the record the coordinator receives. `TabSortZone#getVesselConversionSensor` → `onConvertIn(record)` hands the park the **sensor's** record, which is sampled from `me.vesselConversionSourceRect`. `resolveRemoteDragTransition` returns only a copy, and the coordinator's target-proxy sizing is that copy's only reader. Changing the copy's extent to the tab header's therefore does not touch the park, so AC-1 as you wrote it is safe.

The implementation keeps your shape: the engaged transition record's extent becomes the dragged tab header's. I rename the field `proxyRect`, so its name says what it sizes. It also carries the grab offset inside the tab (point 2 stands, though it bites only after a re-show the platform clamped). Points 3 and 4 stand.
